A page from an explorer's field sketchbook, drawn on the spot, in the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries (Cook's artists, Conrad Martens on the Beagle, Thomas Baines with Livingstone, Edward Wilson in the Antarctic). A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink over parts of it, with loose parallel hatching for shade; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green and faded blue, pooling and leaving the paper bare in places. The drawing is unfinished: detail is concentrated on the city, and the edges, the sky and the near water dissolve into bare cream paper in an irregular vignette. Slightly foxed, worn sketchbook paper with soft tone variation; a single page, no binding or spine visible. An observed working sketch, not a finished painting. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, dates or signature. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given.

View: A wide panoramic view of the peninsula of the city seen from the Asian shore across the mouth of the Bosporus, looking west in early morning light, with the low sun behind the viewer lighting the city from the east (no sun in the sky). The Sea of Marmara opens on the left; the point of the peninsula (Seraglio Point) sits left of centre with the sea walls along its shore; the city climbs over low hills to the right; the inlet of the Golden Horn opens on the right with the hill of Galata beyond it at the far right edge. Calm water with boats fills the foreground third of the picture.

This picture: Around 450 CE. A large late-Roman city covering the whole peninsula: long sea walls with towers along the shore, the curved end of the Hippodrome with its arcades near the point, a tall column with a statue on top rising above the forum, early Christian basilicas with long pitched roofs (no great domes yet), the arches of an aqueduct striding between two hills, dense houses with tiled roofs, Roman galleys and merchant ships in the foreground. A small walled suburb on the Galata hill.
